newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish rights activist faces separatism charges.
newsitem.headline: Turkish rights activist faces separatism charges.

text.p: A Turkish state security court on Thursday opened the trial of a rights activist facing charges of spreading separatist propaganda in a book he wrote on the history of human rights.

The charges against Erol Anar, deputy general secretary of Turkey's human rights association, centre on a chapter entitled "The Kurdish question" in his book, confiscated three months ago soon after publication, his lawyer Ercan Kanar said.
"This case is a crime committed by the state against the people," Kanar, also a rights activist, told Reuters.
Anar faces a possible three years in prison if found guilty of the charges under controversial article eight of Turkey's anti-terror law which outlaws "separatist propaganda."
Separatist Kurdish rebels have for the last 12 years waged an armed struggle for autonomy or independence in Turkey's southeast. Over 20,000 people have died in the fighting.

The trial follows Amnesty International's launch on Wednesday of a world-wide campaign highlighting human rights abuses in Turkey and seeking the repeal or reform of the anti-terror law's eighth article.
